title: Iterative Fiber Depth-First Walker (Without Recursion)
concept: Depth-First Search using child, sibling, return Pointers
problemStatement: Implement `traverseFiberTree(rootFiber, visitor)` that visits every Fiber node in depth-first pre-order using ONLY `child`, `sibling`, and `return` pointers. Must not use recursion or array stack frames.
interviewTrap: This is the exact workLoop algorithm of React's Concurrent Scheduler. If you use recursion, deep component trees exhaust call stack memory.

testCases.name: Visits parent before children (pre-order)
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'root', child: null }; const a = { id: 'A', return: root, child: null, sibling: null }; const b = { id: 'B', return: root, child: null, sibling: null }; root.child = a; a.sibling = b; const order = []; traverseFiberTree(root, f => order.push(f.id)); return order;

testCases.name: Navigates deeply nested subtrees
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'root', child: null }; const b = { id: 'B', return: root, child: null, sibling: null }; const a1 = { id: 'A1', child: null, sibling: null }; const a = { id: 'A', return: root, child: a1, sibling: b }; a1.return = a; root.child = a; const order = []; traverseFiberTree(root, f => order.push(f.id)); return order;

testCases.name: Terminates cleanly on single root node
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'solo', child: null, sibling: null, return: null }; const order = []; traverseFiberTree(root, f => order.push(f.id)); return order;

details.name: Terminates cleanly on single root node

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React represents UI as a singly linked list of Fiber nodes (`child`, `sibling`, `return`). Render phase is interruptible and can be paused; commit phase is strictly synchronous.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Depth-First Search using child, sibling, return Pointers.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Depth-First Search using child, sibling, return Pointers is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: This is the exact workLoop algorithm of React's Concurrent Scheduler. If you use recursion, deep component trees exhaust call stack memory.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Walk through the workLoop algorithm using child, sibling, and return pointers.
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: 1) `beginWork(node)`: descend to `node.child` if it exists. 2) If no child, `completeWork(node)`: check `node.sibling`. If sibling exists, pivot to sibling and repeat step 1. 3) If no sibling, ascend to `node.return`, complete parent, and check parent's sibling. 4) Terminate when reaching root with no siblings.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The ultimate React Fiber traversal algorithm question.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does this iterative traversal allow React to pause work during Concurrent Mode?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Because traversal is an iterative `while` loop tracking a single global pointer `workInProgress`, pausing is as simple as saving the current pointer and breaking out of the loop: `if (shouldYield()) break;`. When the browser has idle time, React calls `workLoop()` and picks up exactly from `workInProgress` without unwinding.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of how linked lists enable cooperative multitasking.

realWorldUseCases.description: The core engine loop driving React 18/19 concurrent rendering.

howToExplain.opening: React reconciles components using an iterative Depth-First Search over child, sibling, and return pointers, enabling interruptible, time-sliced rendering.
keyPoints: Can pause at any unit of work and resume without losing position.
howToExplain.closingImpression: By removing recursive call frames, React achieved the holy grail of UI engineering: interruptible rendering.
analogies: Exploring a cave with a rope: you walk in (child), check side passages (sibling), and backtrack along the rope (return). You can drop the rope for lunch and pick it up right where you stood.

commonMistakes.why: Recursion defeats the entire purpose of Fiber: recursive calls cannot be paused or yielded.
commonMistakes.correct: Always use an iterative while loop with pointer assignments.

followUpDeepDive.question: What are Effect Flags (flags & subtreeFlags) in modern React Fibers?
followUpDeepDive.answer: In React 18+, `flags` stores bitwise mutations (Placement, Update, Deletion) on the fiber. `subtreeFlags` aggregates whether any descendant in the subtree has pending mutations, allowing React to skip traversing entire clean subtrees in O(1) time.
